chunks: From him, from Imran ibn Musa, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid al-Kazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from al-Hakam al-Hannat, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, who said:

I asked Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him): 'By what manner did Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) travel [conduct himself]?' He said: 'Indeed, Abu al-Yaqdhan was a sharp-minded man, may God have mercy on him. He said: O Commander of the Faithful, by what manner will you travel [conduct yourself] with these people tomorrow?' He said: 'With al-Man (Generosity/Bestowal), just as the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) traveled with the people of Mecca.'
ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib conduct himself when dealing with the people of Mecca?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the strategic wisdom of Imam Ali’s governance by linking his conduct to the Prophet’s diplomatic approach during the Conquest of Mecca. The term 'al-Man' signifies a style of leadership characterized by magnanimity and bestowing favors to win hearts, a principle deeply valued in Shia political ethics as a means of consolidating authority through grace rather than force.
